description: Kung Pao Chicken Sichuan is a fiery and flavorful stir-fry, a true masterpiece of Sichuan cuisine known for its distinctive 'mala' or numbing and spicy taste. Tender chicken pieces are wok-fried with crunchy peanuts, aromatic Sichuan peppercorns, and dried chilies, all coated in a glossy, savory-sweet sauce. This iconic dish offers an exhilarating balance of heat, sweetness, and tang, making it a beloved staple worldwide.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the cubed chicken with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch, 1 tablespoon of light soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon of sesame oil. Mix thoroughly to ensure all chicken pieces are coated. Let it marinate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 30 minutes for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Kung Pao Sauce
instructions.text: In a separate small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons of light soy sauce, 1 teaspoon of dark soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of Chinese black vinegar, 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar, 1 tablespoon of Shaoxing wine, 1 tablespoon of cornstarch, and 2 tablespoons of chicken broth. Stir until the cornstarch is fully dissolved and the sauce is smooth. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large wok or heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, making sure not to overcrowd the wok. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside on a clean plate.

instructions.title: Infuse Aromatics and Chilies
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry constantly for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and the chilies darken slightly, being very careful not to burn them, which can make them bitter.

instructions.title: Sauté Garlic, Ginger, and Green Onions
instructions.text: Immediately add the minced garlic, minced ginger, and the white and light green parts of the sliced green onions to the wok. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes until aromatic, ensuring not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Combine and Thicken the Sauce
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken to the wok with the infused aromatics. Give the prepared Kung Pao sauce a quick stir to re-mix the cornstarch, then pour it evenly over the ingredients in the wok. Stir continuously for 3-5 minutes, allowing the sauce to simmer and thicken, coating all the chicken and vegetables beautifully. The sauce should become glossy and adhere to the ingredients.

instructions.title: Add Peanuts and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the unsalted roasted peanuts during the last minute of cooking. Toss everything together to combine. Garnish with the reserved green onion tops if desired, and serve immediately with steamed white rice for a truly authentic Chinese meal.

tips: For extra tender chicken, a technique called 'velveting' can be used. After marinating, blanch the chicken in hot oil for 30 seconds or boil in water for 1-2 minutes before stir-frying. This helps seal in moisture.

The quality of your Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies is crucial for authentic flavor. Toasting the peppercorns lightly before use can enhance their numbing aroma. Adjust the quantity of chilies to your preferred spice level.

Kung Pao Chicken is best served immediately after cooking to enjoy the crisp texture of the peanuts and the vibrant flavors. It pairs perfectly with plain steamed white rice to balance the richness and spice.
